official.deadline_note: Receiving institutions set earlier internal deadlines (Wuhan University's Spring 2027 one-semester track closed 25 October 2026). For September entry the centre's student deadline is 15 May with institutional review by 25 May; four-week July-entry applications close 15 April and December-entry applications close 15 September.
official.application_cycle: 2026/2027 cycle: applications for March 2027 entry opened 10 September 2026 and close 31 October 2026; the September 2026 entry round closed 15 May 2026 and the next September-entry round is expected to open 1 March 2027
official.status_note: The current round is the one-semester research programme for March 2027 entry: student applications accepted since 10 September 2026 until 31 October 2026 (Beijing time), with the centre's expert panel finishing review about three months before enrolment. The September 2026 entry round has closed (student deadline was 15 May 2026).
official.tuition_coverage_note: Published wording: the scholarship covers tuition, accommodation, living allowance (four-week researchers excluded) and comprehensive medical insurance; the tuition is pooled by the receiving institution for the scholar's training and management, cultural activities and Chinese proficiency testing. Online programmes receive tuition funding only.
benefits: Full tuition, pooled by the receiving institution for the scholar's training and management, cultural activities and Chinese proficiency test organisation (online programmes are funded for tuition only)

Free on-campus accommodation, generally a double room; if the scholar is approved to live off campus, the institution pays an accommodation allowance monthly or quarterly - CNY 1,000 per month for doctoral students and CNY 700 per month for other scholarship students

Monthly living allowance paid by the receiving institution: CNY 2,500 per month for undergraduates and one-academic-year and one-semester research students; CNY 3,000 per month for MA students in International Chinese Language Education; CNY 3,500 per month for PhD students in International Chinese Language Education (four-week research students are excluded)

Comprehensive medical insurance purchased by the receiving institution: CNY 100 per person for four-week students, CNY 400 per person for one-semester students, CNY 800 per person per year for programmes of one academic year or longer
eligibility: Non-Chinese citizens; applicants of Chinese origin (naturalised former Chinese citizens and their foreign-national children) must pass a nationality pre-screening at the admission stage
Friendly toward China, with no criminal record, and willing to abide by Chinese laws, regulations and institutional rules
Physically and mentally healthy, of excellent character and academic standing
Committed to pursuing Chinese-language education, teaching or related work
Aged 16-35 (reckoned at 1 September of the entry year); in-service Chinese-language teachers up to 45; undergraduate applicants generally not over 25
requirements: PhD in International Chinese Language Education (4 years, September entry): master's degree in teaching Chinese as a foreign language, linguistics, International Chinese Language Education or an education-related field; HSK Level 6 score 200 plus HSKK Advanced 60, or HSK Level 7
MA in International Chinese Language Education (2 years, September entry): bachelor's degree; HSK Level 5 score 210 plus HSKK Intermediate 60
BA in Chinese Language and Literature / International Chinese Language Education (4 years, September entry): high-school diploma; HSK Level 4 score 210 plus HSKK Intermediate 60

One-academic-year research student (11 months, September entry): International Chinese Education direction HSK Level 3 score 270 with an HSKK score; Chinese Language and Literature direction HSK Level 4 score 180 with HSKK Intermediate 60; Chinese language study direction HSK Level 3 score 210 (HSKK preferred)
One-semester research student (5 months, September or March entry): International Chinese Education / Chinese Language and Literature directions HSK Level 3 score 180 with an HSKK score
Four-week research student (4 weeks, July or December entry): any HSK score; group nomination of 10-15 students per cohort by the recommending institution
documents: Scan of the passport photo page
HSK and HSKK score reports valid within the last two years

Recommendation letter from the head of an authorised recommending institution (Confucius Institute, independent Confucius Classroom, designated Chinese test venue, foreign educational institution, university Chinese department, overseas Chinese-teaching body, or Chinese embassy/consulate)
Highest diploma (or expected-graduation certificate) and per-semester academic transcripts for degree programmes

Two recommendation letters from associate professors or above for MA and PhD applicants; PhD applicants also submit a Chinese personal statement with a proposed research plan of about 3,000 characters and a supervising professor's acceptance letter
In-service Chinese-language teachers add an employment certificate and recommendation letter from the employer; applicants under 18 submit a notarised guardian commitment
selection_criteria: Central expert-panel review commissioned by the centre, based on HSK and HSKK levels and scores with consideration of country balance
Priority for applicants presenting a post-graduation teaching work agreement or related proof
In-service Chinese-language teachers are prioritised under equal conditions
One-semester and one-academic-year programmes generally exclude applicants who received the same scholarship within the previous three years
An applicant may hold only one Chinese government-institution scholarship at a time; duplicate applications are void
coverage: Accommodation (住宿费) - free on-campus double room, or a monthly allowance if approved to live off campus
Living allowance (生活费) - paid monthly by the receiving institution, four-week research students excluded
Comprehensive medical insurance (综合医疗保险费)
application_method: Secure a recommendation from an authorised recommending institution such as the local Confucius Institute or Confucius Classroom
Register and submit the application with document uploads on the centre's scholarship system (cis.chinese.cn, also reachable from the scholarship section of www.chinese.cn)
Where the receiving university requires it, file a parallel application on the university's own portal (e.g. Wuhan University)
Track the review progress online; after the award, confirm enrolment procedures with the receiving university, print the award certificate and register by the date on the admission notice
official.application_route: Online application through the official cis.chinese.cn system with a nomination from an authorised recommending institution, plus any parallel application the chosen receiving university requires
official.study_mode: Full-time, in-person study in China (online programmes receive tuition funding only)
official.citizenship_residency: Non-Chinese citizens aged 16-35 reckoned at 1 September of the entry year; in-service Chinese-language teachers up to 45; applicants of Chinese origin must clear a nationality pre-screening
official.international_eligibility: Yes - open to non-Chinese citizens worldwide through authorised recommending institutions; the centre balances selection by country
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: International Chinese Language Education and related Chinese-language fields; the applicant must be recommended by an authorised body (Confucius Institute, Confucius Classroom, Chinese test venue, university Chinese department, overseas Chinese-teaching organisation or Chinese embassy/consulate) - not every Confucius Institute holds an allocation
official.research_requirement: MA applicants submit a study plan of 800 or more Chinese characters; PhD applicants submit a Chinese personal statement with a proposed research plan of about 3,000 characters plus a supervising professor's acceptance letter
official.duration: Four weeks / five months (one semester) / eleven months (one academic year) / two years (MA) / four years (BA and PhD)
official.description: Established by the Center for Language Education and Cooperation of the Ministry of Education to meet growing global demand for Chinese-education professionals, promote Chinese-language education worldwide and support the growth of international Chinese-education talent, the scholarship - formerly the Confucius Institute Scholarship - focuses on cultivating qualified overseas Chinese-language teachers. Authorised recommending institutions nominate outstanding students and in-service Chinese-language teachers to study International Chinese Language Education and related programmes at 236 designated Chinese receiving universities.
official.region: China (study destination); applicants from all regions
official.program_type: Chinese government scholarship administered by the Ministry of Education's Center for Language Education and Cooperation - degree and non-degree Chinese-language teacher training

applicant_utility.summary: China's flagship government scholarship for training overseas Chinese-language teachers, run by the Ministry of Education's Center for Language Education and Cooperation, funds full tuition, free on-campus accommodation, a CNY 2,500-3,500 monthly stipend and comprehensive medical insurance at 236 designated universities. You cannot apply directly: you first need a recommendation letter from an authorised body such as a local Confucius Institute, then register on cis.chinese.cn and, at many universities, file a second application with the university itself. The most realistic entry points are the one-semester (HSK 3) and one-year (HSK 3-4) research tracks, while degree tracks demand HSK 4-6 with exact sub-score cut-offs. The live round targets March 2027 entry and closes 31 October 2026 Beijing time, with universities often closing earlier.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-Chinese nationals aged 16-35 with valid HSK/HSKK scores who want a fully funded period of Chinese-language or teacher-training study in China and can obtain a nomination from a local Confucius Institute or similar body
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your local Confucius Institute actually holds an allocation for the current cycle and obtain the institution head's recommendation letter before anything else - without it the online form cannot proceed
Open the official 2026 host-institution table on cis.chinese.cn and check that your target university has a star for your category (research, BA, MA, PhD) - not all 236 hosts take every track
Book HSK/HSKK early: scores must sit inside the two-year validity window and hit the exact sub-score thresholds (for example HSK 4 at 210 plus HSKK Intermediate 60 for the BA track)
Diary both deadlines - the centre's 31 October 2026 cut-off for March 2027 entry and your university's earlier internal one (Wuhan closed 25 October)
Arrange notarised translations of your diploma and full per-semester transcripts, plus a notarised guardian commitment if you are under 18
common_rejection_risks: Applying without an authorised recommending institution - direct applications are not accepted, and not every Confucius Institute has quota
HSK/HSKK reports older than two years or sitting just below the sub-score threshold, which fails the category condition
Choosing a university whose row has no star for your track, or missing the university's parallel application where one is required
Having held the same scholarship within the previous three years, which bars the one-semester and one-year tracks
Incomplete sets (missing transcripts or the head-of-institution letter), any falsified material, or holding another Chinese government scholarship simultaneously - all void the award
BA applicants over 25 and in-service teachers over 45 fall outside the age ceilings for their route
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: International airfare to China, visa and residence-permit fees, and all personal spending beyond the stipend; the four-week track pays no living allowance, so it is effectively tuition-plus-accommodation only, and off-campus students must cover any rent above the CNY 700-1,000 monthly allowance
document_audit: HSK/HSKK reports are checked against the two-year validity window - expired scores are the most common silent failure
Degree applicants need per-semester transcripts pinned to the diploma, not a diploma alone
In-service teachers swap HSK for an employment certificate plus recommendation letter but must stay inside the 45-year ceiling
Applicants of Chinese origin must clear a nationality pre-screening at the admission stage; failing it forfeits the award and any university place
If an expected-graduation letter is submitted, the formal diploma and transcripts must be produced before registration
Under-18 applicants need a notarised guardianship commitment naming a resident guarantor in China
alerts: All deadlines run on Beijing time and the university's internal cut-off is usually earlier than the centre's central one
The stipend is halved if you register after the 15th of the month, stopped during absences from China longer than 15 days, and stopped on withdrawal, suspension or disciplinary action
Results are published only about three months before enrolment, so plan the visa appointment around a late decision
You may hold only one Chinese government scholarship at a time - parallel Chinese-government applications are voided once discovered
A failed entry medical examination, unreported late arrival, withdrawal or suspension cancels the scholarship outright
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Nomination letter from an authorised recommending institution, online registration and document upload on cis.chinese.cn, review by the receiving university (plus its own portal where required), the centre's expert-panel decision about three months out, then confirmation with the university, printing the award certificate and in-person registration on the admission-notice date
